title: Small-etale module comparisons on algebraic-space tests of a fibred category
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids: cartesian lifts of all base arrows exist and every arrow is cartesian. Give $\mathcal C$ the big fppf ringed site of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-pc-fppf-site], with $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(y)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for an object over $T$. Let $K$ be any module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An algebraic-space test $z:V\to\mathcal C$ means a functor over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ from the discrete fibred category of an algebraic space $V$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the restriction functor $K\mapsto K_z$ and, for $a:V\to W$, a test $w:W\to\mathcal C$, and a two-isomorphism $\theta:z\Rightarrow w\circ a$, the canonical tensor comparison $c_{a,\theta}^K:a^*K_w\to K_z$ of [def-sfb-space-test-module-restriction-comparison]. The comparison is natural in $K$ and in the tests and their two-isomorphisms, is the identity for an identity arrow, and respects composition: for $b:W\to B$ and $\eta:w\Rightarrow v\circ b$, $$c_{ba,(\eta a)\theta}^K=c_{a,\theta}^K\circ a^*c_{b,\eta}^K$$ under $(ba)^*\simeq a^*b^*$. On a scheme test it is the map adjoint to ordinary restriction along the corresponding arrow of $\mathcal C$; it is an isomorphism for etale $a$. For a quasi-coherent $K$, in the local-presentation sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], every $K_z$ is quasi-coherent and every $c_{a,\theta}^K$ is an isomorphism, for arbitrary $a$. No stack, algebraicity, flatness or finiteness hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ or the tests is required.

source.place: Tag 075D (lemma-comparison), (1)--(4), and its module extension equation-comparison-modules; Tag 076R (equation-comparison-algebraic-spaces-modules), and the following sentence extending (1)--(4) to algebraic-space tests; Tags 06WH (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent) and 0GQD (lemma-compare-quasi-coherent), including pullback compatibility, for the quasi-coherent clause.

proof.text: First regard $K$ as a big-etale module: every jointly surjective etale scheme family is fppf, since etale means flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fppf-site]. For a test $z$, precomposition with its functor is a big-fppf module by [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]. Its restriction to the etale charts of $V$ is $K_z$. A covering of an etale chart consists of etale scheme maps, and its iterated fibre products give the same diagram in the fibred category under $z$. Thus the sheaf equalizer for $K$ gives precisely the sheaf equalizer for $K_z$. The actions are those of $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and the restrictions are semilinear, so this is a module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The required scheme fibre products and etale composition assertions are [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests].

source.place: Tags 06TS, 06WE; the restriction construction before Tag 075D and the algebraic-space restriction preceding Tag 076R

proof.text: Construct the adjoint map $d:K_w\to a_*K_z$. For an etale scheme $e:E\to W$ and an object $(t:T\to V,r:T\to E)$ of the chart category $\mathcal A(a,E)$, one has $at=er$. The two-isomorphism $\theta$ and the arrow induced by $r$ give an arrow $\alpha_{T,r}:z(t)\to w(e)$ over $r$. Send $m\in K_w(E)=K(w(e))$ to $K(\alpha_{T,r})(m)\in K_z(T)$. This is $\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)$-linear. For a chart arrow $q:T'\to T$, naturality of $\theta$ gives $\alpha_{T',rq}=\alpha_{T,r}\circ z(q)$, so the images are compatible. The limiting-cone property in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] gives $d_E$. The same formula after a map $E'\to E$ proves compatibility with restrictions; hence $d$ is a module map. Take its adjoint $c_{a,\theta}^K:a^*K_w\to K_z$. By [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], on local chart tensors its formula is $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,K(\alpha_{T,r})(m)$. This is balanced because $K(\alpha_{T,r})(sm)=r^\sharp(s)\,K(\alpha_{T,r})(m)$. This construction uses the limit vertex specified in the cited definition, not an assumption that the category of all charts is small.

source.place: Tag 076R (equation-comparison-algebraic-spaces-modules); the adjoint construction immediately before it

proof.text: For a module map $h:K\to L$, naturality on the arrow $\alpha$ says $h_zK(\alpha)=L(\alpha)h_w$; linearity therefore makes the two comparison squares equal on $b\otimes m$. Identity tests give $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ and $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$. For composable tests, take local chart tensors $u\otimes(s\otimes m)$ for $a^*b^*K_v$, with $u$ a function on a chart $T$ of $V$ and $s$ a function on a chart $E'$ of $W$ receiving the chart map $r:T\to E'$. Write $\alpha$ for the arrow over the chart map to $W$, and $\beta$ for that over the chart map to $B$. Naturality of the two-isomorphisms identifies the arrow of the composite two-isomorphism $(\eta a)\theta$ with $\beta\circ\alpha$. Successive comparisons send this tensor to $u\,K(\alpha)(s\,K(\beta)(m))=u\,r^\sharp(s)\,K(\beta\circ\alpha)(m)$. The tensor-composition map of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] sends it first to $u\,r^\sharp(s)\otimes m$, so the direct comparison has the same value. Maps out of a tensor pullback are determined by their adjoints, hence by these chart-unit values, which gives the stated composition equation. Replacing a test by a two-isomorphic one applies $K$ to the components of that isomorphism; its naturality gives the same commuting square with every $\alpha$. These formulas prove naturality in tests, two-isomorphisms, and $K$, including the identity laws.

source.place: Tag 075D (lemma-comparison), (1), (3), (4), and their extension following Tag 076R

proof.text: For scheme tests, an object $E\to W$ pulls back to the etale scheme $E\times_WV\to V$. Projection of the cone in step 2 to this chart is exactly the restriction along the corresponding cartesian lift in $\mathcal C$. By step 1, $K$ is a big-etale module, and the identification $\tau$ of the specified adjoint with ringed tensor pullback [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] is fixed by the units, so the adjoint of this cone is the scheme comparison of [lem-sfb-fibred-big-etale-restriction-calculus], since that statement specifies precisely this restriction-induced comparison. Thus our map is the required scheme-test map. If $a:V\to W$ is etale, tensor pullback is restriction on the localized etale sites by [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. Every etale scheme $t:T\to V$ is then also an etale chart of $W$ [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. On it our map is $K$ applied to $\theta_T:z(t)\simeq w(at)$, with the tensor unit identification $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$ of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. Its inverse is induced by $\theta_T^{-1}$. These inverses commute with restrictions by naturality of $\theta$, proving the etale assertion for arbitrary modules.

source.place: Tag 075D (2), equation-comparison-modules, and the extension following Tag 076R

proof.text: Now suppose $K$ is quasi-coherent. For every etale scheme test $t:T\to V$, [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] gives a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_{z(t)}$, whose associated etale sheaf is the restriction of $K_z$ to $T_{\mathrm{et}}$: for an etale $q:T'\to T$ both have value $\Gamma(T',q^*F_{z(t)})=K(z(tq))$, with the same restrictions. The associated etale sheaf is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Unpack [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]: its local presentations on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ are presentations on the slice $V_{\mathrm{et}}/T$, with the same structure ring and module. Indeed every map between etale scheme charts over $V$ is etale and their composites are etale [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Thus for every object $T$ of $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ there is a covering on which $K_z$ has a presentation by small sums of the structure sheaf. This is exactly quasi-coherence of $K_z$, and applies to each test.

source.place: Tags 06WH, 06WI and 0GQD; the chartwise argument of lemma-compare-locally-quasi-coherent

proof.text: Finally take arbitrary $a:V\to W$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $E\to W$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its pullback $V_E\to V$ is a surjective etale cover, and choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $T\to V_E$. These facts and composition are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Let $r:T\to E$ be the resulting scheme map, with no flatness condition. The tensor-pullback restriction isomorphism of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] and composition identify the restriction of $a^*K_w$ to $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $r^*(K_w|_{E_{\mathrm{et}}})$. By step 3 and the etale identifications of step 4, the restriction of $c_{a,\theta}$ is the scheme comparison for $r$ (the two-isomorphism is the restriction of $\theta$). The latter is invertible: [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] gives the canonical isomorphism $r^*F_{w(E)}\simeq F_{z(T)}$, and [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] turns it into an isomorphism $r_{\mathrm{et}}^*(F_{w(E)})_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq(F_{z(T)})_{\mathrm{et}}$; both this isomorphism and the scheme comparison send the chart-unit tensor $1\otimes m$ to the restriction of $m$ along the arrow over $r$, so they are equal. Thus $c_{a,\theta}$ is invertible on the etale cover $T\to V$. To see this suffices, on every etale scheme $D\to V$ pull back that cover; the local inverses agree on double overlaps, being inverses of the same restricted map. The sheaf equalizer glues them uniquely, compatibly with $D$ and its restrictions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. They give a global inverse. No step imposed algebraicity on $\mathcal C$ or flatness or finiteness on $a$.
